title: Morgan Stanley Just Put a $54 Target on This AI-Pivoting Bitcoin Miner. Amazon Is Already a Customer
excerpt: Cipher Digital’s transformation from Bitcoin miner to AI-infrastructure landlord is becoming easier to value because the company now has a real hyperscaler c...
content_html:
Cipher Digital's transformation from Bitcoin miner to AI-infrastructure landlord is becoming easier to value because the company now has a real hyperscaler customer. Morgan Stanley raised its price target on September 18 to $54 from $43.50 while keeping an Overweight rating. A major asset supporting Cipher's AI-infrastructure thesis is a 15-year, roughly $5.5 billion lease at Cipher's Black Pearl site with Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). For Cipher Digital Inc. (NASDAQ:CIFR), the trade is no longer simply that old mining sites might someday host AI. It is whether long-term cloud contracts can justify the capital required to turn power into data-center capacity.

Amazon gives the pivot a customer, not just a narrative

Cipher Digital Inc. (NASDAQ:CIFR) agreed to provide about 300 megawatts at Black Pearl to Amazon Web Services under a 15-year arrangement. Cipher began delivering capacity in August 2026, two months ahead of schedule, and said rent had commenced. Cipher also has a separate Barber Lake transaction backed by Google, which adds another hyperscaler validation point. The bull case is that powered sites with interconnection rights have become scarce enough that Cipher can monetize land and electricity at infrastructure-like contract values rather than crypto-cycle multiples.

The bear case is financing and execution. A long lease only becomes valuable after the data center is built, commissioned and delivered on schedule. Construction overruns, equipment lead times or a higher cost of capital can eat into returns before rent starts. Cipher's legacy mining exposure also means investors are underwriting a business-model transition while new projects consume cash.

Amazon gets another route to scarce power

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) benefits because AWS can secure capacity without developing every site itself. Its AI demand is already pushing companywide capital spending higher, so long-term leases can trade ownership risk for contractual commitments. The risk is the same one facing every hyperscaler: capacity contracted during a shortage can look expensive if hardware becomes more efficient or AI demand grows more slowly than expected.

Insider Monkey's database counted 72 hedge funds holding Cipher in Q2 2026, up from 49 in Q1. D. E. Shaw's disclosed common-share position was about 14.51 million shares after decreasing 12%, while its call exposure was larger. Amazon's hedge-fund count rose to 369 in Q2 from 353 in Q1, and Arrowstreet Capital increased its position about 24% to 40.35 million shares. The filings predate Morgan Stanley's September target change.
